title: Scalar comparison of compact-support system Hom
statement:
theorem integralDualizing_support_system_hom_comparison
    (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E X)
    (G : CoefPairingSystem l E (finiteDualizingCompactification D X) S) :
    Nonempty (integralDualizingSupportSystemHom D l E X S G ≅
      (integralDualizingCompactSections l E D hl X).op ⋙
        integralDualizingCoefficientHomTower l E)

source.place: Second proof paragraph: finite mapping-complex comparisons and reduction-compatible counits.

proof.text: For a fixed constructible input, residue Tor invariance supplies a common finite Tor interval. Choose a finite dimension bound for the finite-type scheme. Prescribed compact-support reduction identifies its quotient-system compact support with the scalar extension of its integral compact-support value. The comparisons use the actual reduction projections and commute with every quotient transition.

Point-section reduction identifies the point-system scalar extension with tensor of the actual integral section complex by the quotient ring system. Scalar tensor-restriction adjunction on that sequence site identifies Hom into its regular quotient unit with Hom from constant integral sections into the restricted quotient tower.

The constant K-flat input and one simultaneous K-injective resolution of the quotient tower compute this Hom as Hom(P,I_n) with its actual transitions. Uniqueness of the tensor right adjoint and of localization identifies it with integralDualizingCoefficientHomTower. The same comparison commutes with precomposition before localization, proving naturality rather than merely objectwise invertibility.
